text:
alex: FYI — enterprise customer reported a regression: streaming responses look fast for first byte but total response time p99 is ~3-4x higher than non-streaming. They see a lot of mid-stream pauses.

maria: customer, ACME-Cloud (redacted tenant id), sent request examples. They said switching to non-streaming reduces p99 by ~60%.

sam: can you paste their curl/sdk repro?

alex: here, from their support email:
```
# streaming (SSE)
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \ 
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \ 
  'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/stream?model=rw-13b'
# non-streaming
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \ 
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \ 
  'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate?model=rw-13b'
```
They included a p99 trace: first-chunk at 120ms but long gaps between chunks, total ~2.8s.

ops-bot: note: tenant override flags: chunk_coalesce=enabled, flush_window_ms=40, edge_mux=on

tj: interesting — we've had a coalesce change last week (eng-runtime) that groups small partial chunks to reduce syscall overhead. That raises TTFB for tiny responses but can increase inter-chunk latency if the model or kernel stalls.

maria: customer timeline aligns with the kernel patch rollout on 3/12 to canary then 3/14 prod. They upgraded to runtime v1.12.4.

sam: quick triage steps: (1) confirm if coalescing is active on their route, (2) reproduce on dedicated env with seq lengths + batch shape, (3) try disabling coalescing for tenant and see impact.

alex: I toggled chunk_coalesce=false for their tenant via admin-config and asked them to retry. Waiting on results. Workaround offered: non-streaming mode or pass `?stream=false` in SDK to avoid chunk stalls.

sam: also ask them to send a raw stream capture (tcpdump or curl --raw) so we can see exact chunk boundaries. The difference between kernel kv-cache flushes vs proxy coalesce will show up.

maria: customer replied — disabling coalesce dropped p99 from 2.8s to 1.1s. They can tolerate that but want a proper fix.

tj: that's a strong signal coalesce is the regressor. Proposed mitigations:
- short-term: keep tenant-level disable and revert global coalesce rollout to canary
- mid-term: implement heuristic: if model latency variance > threshold, reduce coalesce window or switch to immediate flush for small chunks
- long-term: make kernel backpressure signals available to proxy so we don't coalesce in presence of mid-token stalls

alex: I'm going to open an ENG-RUNTIME bug with the reproduction steps and attach the customer's raw stream. Will request a hotfix roll-back if we see more tenants impacted.

sam: +1. Can we also add a dashboard to detect streaming p95/p99 ratio vs non-streaming for new rollouts? If ratio > 1.5, auto-alert.

maria: filed support ticket S-2026, noted workaround and tenant flag change. ENG ticket RT-431 opened (assign tj).

ops-bot: action logged: support:S-2026 created by maria at 4567891500, eng:RT-431 created and assigned to tj

tj: I will reproduce locally today with rw-13b config and 0/1/2-token emission variance workloads. If confirmed, patch to add per-route adaptive flush_window_ms and a kill-switch for global coalesce.

alex: customer asked for ETA — I'll give a conservative "48-72h" and keep tenant flag as the safe setting.

sam: note to oncall: if you see surge of similar tickets after runtime updates, please flip `coalesce` back at cluster level and notify infra.

maria: customer appreciates quick workaround. Closing loop once eng confirms root cause and plan. :thumbsup:

alex: attaching the raw snippet they sent (sanitized):
```
:event: chunk
data: {"tokens": "hello"}

:event: chunk
data: {"tokens": " world"}
(45s gap)
:event: chunk
data: {"tokens": "!"}
```
This long gap is consistent with a kernel stall or mis-tuned coalescer.

tj: thanks — will post findings in RT-431 when I have them. If anybody else sees similar tenant regressions, please merge into RT-431 to avoid duplicate bugs.

alex: cool. keeping tenant flag disabled. I'll update the customer in the morning with patch plan.
